filings.title: Polyfill: Validate result in UTC fast path in GetPossibleEpochNanoseconds
filings.summary: Near the end of the supported range, a calculation in the UTC time zone that should throw a RangeError instead silently returns a wrong value, because GetPossibleEpochNanoseconds' UTC fast path skips the range check every other time zone path makes.

filings.title: Polyfill: Update Meiji era start date
filings.summary: The Japanese calendar gives dates from 1868 to the end of 1872 the Meiji era instead of the Gregorian-equivalent ce/bce era the spec requires, so era and era-year fields for that period are wrong.

filings.title: Polyfill: Fix extreme PlainYearMonth crash in non-ISO calendars
filings.summary: Converting an in-range Hebrew, Islamic, coptic-family, or Indian calendar date near either end of the supported range throws 'Invalid ISO date', even though the requested date itself is valid.

filings.title: Don't format dates past the range limit when counting months in until()
filings.summary: Counting months between two non-ISO calendar dates throws when the second date falls in the last (or first) month of the supported range, because the month-by-month loop builds and formats an out-of-range date it doesn't actually need.

filings.title: Search the last partial window when looking for the next time zone transition
filings.summary: Looking up the next time zone transition within about the last two months before the maximum Instant can return null even though a transition exists there, which then makes startOfDay, hoursInDay, and toZonedDateTime throw a TypeError instead of returning the right result.

filings.title: Start the time zone transition search before the first transition in 1844
filings.summary: Time zone transition lookups before 1847 miss a real transition on 1844-12-31 in five zones (Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones), because the search's historical starting point assumes 1847 is the earliest transition in the tzdb, which is no longer true.

filings.title: Release request: main has fixes that 0.5.1 doesn't (ZonedDateTime near the Instant limits, #341, #347)
filings.summary: Users of the published 0.5.1 release still hit several bugs -- including throwing for valid ZonedDateTime values near both range limits, and two calendar-conversion issues -- that are already fixed 76 commits ahead on main, with no release published to bring the fixes to them.

filings.title: Polyfill: non-ISO until() by months gives wrong results since #3245, and throws near the range limits
filings.summary: Counting months between non-ISO calendar dates gives a wrong, non-round-tripping result at ordinary dates since a recent change, and throws entirely near the range limits.

filings.title: Polyfill: GetNamedTimeZoneNextTransition misses a transition in the last search window before the max Instant
filings.summary: Looking up the next time zone transition in the last search window before the maximum Instant can return null even though a transition exists there, so code that depends on it throws a TypeError instead of getting the right answer.

filings.title: Polyfill: calendarToIsoDate overshoot assertion from #3292 is reachable in coptic/ethiopic/ethioaa month 13
filings.summary: Building a coptic, ethiopic, or ethioaa calendar date in month 13 can hit an internal assertion failure instead of returning the correct date, because a search-loop optimization assumed an 8-day step could never skip over the whole month, which turns out to be reachable for that month, only 5 or 6 days long.
filings.gmtNote: GMT computes coptic and ethiopic dates through ethioaa and finds a date from its calendar fields by bisection, so this search-step bug can't affect it. A canary check (D10) watches for it in every polyfill release.

filings.title: Polyfill: time zone transitions before 1847 are not found (Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones on 1844-12-31)
filings.summary: Time zone transition lookups before 1847 miss a real transition on 1844-12-31 in five zones (Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones), because the search's historical starting point wrongly assumes no zone's tzdb data has a transition before 1847.
